name: medusa
lore:
Whispers echo in the shadowed ruins, tales of creatures born of beauty twisted into monstrous form. Medusae, they are called, their gaze a curse, their hair a writhing nest of vipers. Once, perhaps, they walked as mortals, but now they are beings of fear, their lairs adorned with silent statues, frozen testaments to their deadly power. Beware the glint of red in the dark, for it may be the last thing you ever see.

Imagine stumbling upon a forgotten temple, the air thick with the scent of decay and dust. Statues, eerily lifelike, line the halls, their faces frozen in expressions of horror or surprise. You feel a prickling unease, a sense of being watched. Then, from the shadows, a figure emerges, veiled and cloaked. Her voice, when she speaks, is like the hiss of snakes, and as she removes her veil, you are met with the horrifying truth: a Medusa, her eyes burning with a malevolent light, ready to turn you into another silent monument to her power. 

The tragedy of a medusa is that they know that they are monsters. Their very existence is a curse that not only forces them to live a life of solitude, but to be constantly fearful of their own reflection. Many medusae simply wish to be rid of the curse, but most take out their frustration on anyone they come across, as they are driven mad from the knowledge of the monstrous power they possess.
